subsystems.name: Cryogenic probe station
subsystems.role: holds a whole wafer at low temperature and steps between dies without warming up.

subsystems.name: Cooling plant
subsystems.role: produces the cold: a few kelvin for spin-qubit work, millikelvin where superconducting qubits are involved.
parts: dilution unit and its still/heat exchangers

subsystems.name: Probe card and on-die contacts
subsystems.role: brings hundreds of signal lines down onto micrometre-scale pads.
parts: high-density probe needles or membrane probes

subsystems.name: Signal chain and filtering
subsystems.role: carries microwave pulses in and faint microwave photons out without drowning them in noise.

subsystems.name: Multiplexing electronics
subsystems.role: lets one cooldown measure many qubits rather than one.

subsystems.name: Automation and yield analytics
subsystems.role: turns thousands of individual measurements into wafer maps and distributions.

buildSteps.title: Choose and prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: The prober needs a low-vibration floor slab, a stable electrical supply, helium recovery and shielding from stray radio-frequency fields, because coherence is easily destroyed by interference.

buildSteps.title: Install the cooling plant
buildSteps.detail: A pulse-tube cryocooler with its compressor is mounted below or beside the chamber, then a dilution stage is added if millikelvin operation is required.

buildSteps.title: Fit and calibrate the wafer chuck
buildSteps.detail: The chuck is machined flat to a few micrometres and characterised at operating temperature, because it shrinks as it cools; position encoders are corrected for that shrinkage so dies land under the probes.

buildSteps.title: Design the probe card
buildSteps.detail: Needles or a membrane probe are laid out to match the die's pad pitch, with thin, low-thermal-conductance lines so that contact does not dump heat into the wafer.

buildSteps.title: Wire and filter the signal path
buildSteps.detail: Coaxial looms are routed from room temperature down each cooling stage, with attenuators and filters at every stage to absorb thermal noise before it reaches the device.

buildSteps.title: Add multiplexing and room-temperature electronics
buildSteps.detail: Cryo-CMOS multiplexers and resonators reduce the number of lines needed, while arbitrary-waveform generators, microwave sources and digitizers sit outside the cryostat.

buildSteps.title: Write the test program
buildSteps.detail: Automated routines step across the wafer, contact each die, and run the same measurement sequence: qubit frequency, relaxation and coherence times, and randomised-benchmarking gate fidelity.

buildSteps.title: Validate against known-good devices
buildSteps.detail: A small set of fully characterised dies is re-measured to prove the prober's numbers match a conventional dilution-refrigerator measurement, which is the reference method.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop to the fab
buildSteps.detail: Wafer maps are fed back to lithography, deposition and annealing steps so that process drift is corrected before the next lot.

prerequisites.why: provide the few-kelvin to millikelvin environment the devices need.
contacting hundreds of pads at low temperature without injecting heat or losing signal is still a hard engineering problem.
without on-chip multiplexing, wiring heat and cable count grow faster than the wafer can support.

prerequisites.tech: Reproducible qubit fabrication on large wafers
prerequisites.why: statistical testing is only useful if the process itself is stable enough to be characterised.
measuring coherence and fidelity at speed is routine in single-device labs but must be scaled and made hands-off.

pathway.milestone: full-wafer probing of silicon spin qubits at roughly 1–2 K, where those devices can still operate
pathway.unlocks: hundreds of devices characterised per cooldown instead of a handful, and the first genuine yield maps.

pathway.milestone: millikelvin wafer-scale probing with multiplexed readout for superconducting qubits
pathway.unlocks: statistics on frequency targeting and coherence that multi-qubit processor design depends on.

pathway.milestone: cryogenic testing built into standard fab process control
pathway.unlocks: design rules and specifications based on measured distributions rather than on a few best devices.

pathway.milestone: cryogenic wafer sort producing known-good dies
pathway.unlocks: assembling large quantum processors from pre-tested parts, cutting the cost of packaging and wiring.
